intended_use.summary: Assess exact official incident, reference-availability, HLS metadata, and ecoregion sources for a 2021-2022 Oregon, Washington, and Idaho metadata-only candidate universe. No source is adopted and no scientific source body is opened by this assessment.
planned_actions: adopt exact source revisions after owner approval
query a hash-bound WFIGS snapshot using an explicit field allowlist
download the exact MTBS version 12.0 perimeter archive into controlled custody
query anonymous CMR granule metadata for the exact HLSL30 and HLSS30 collections
download the exact EPA Level III ecoregion archive into controlled custody

sources.name: NIFC WFIGS Interagency Fire Perimeters, ArcGIS item 5e72b1699bf74eefb3f3aff6f4ba5511, FeatureServer layer 0

evidence.note: Public Feature Service item owned by NIFC_Authoritative; exact item ID and service URL observed.
Layer 0 schema version 12 observed; service item ID matches; dataLastEditDate is dynamic and must be rebound at intake.

criteria.note: The source is a dynamic service, not a permanent revision. Intake must bind item ID, schema bytes, query, retrieval time, dataLastEditDate, and returned bytes.

evidence.note: NIFC identifies WFIGS as the authoritative interagency geospatial service and explains IRWIN and FODR provenance.

criteria.note: Authoritative for public best-available interagency incident attribution and perimeters, subject to its documented incompleteness and dynamic updates.

evidence.note: Anonymous public access, query and extract capabilities, JSON/GeoJSON/PBF output, and a 2,000-record page limit were observed.

criteria.note: Use fixed absolute filters and paginated queries. Relative-date queries are prohibited by the publisher warning.

evidence.note: The dataset is public and the custom terms are a no-warranty and proper-use disclaimer rather than an access, reuse, or attribution prohibition.

criteria.note: Approval covers querying selected public factual incident fields and geometry and publishing derived IDs, hashes, counts, and provenance with NIFC attribution. Republishing the complete source service is not proposed.

evidence.note: NIFC states that certified and historic attribution derives from FODR while other records derive from IRWIN; best-available perimeters may combine multiple source systems.

criteria.note: Every retained row must preserve WFIGS GlobalID, source system, source IDs, query, and snapshot identity.

evidence.note: The frozen protocol requires exact source revision, row hashes, retrieval times, and deterministic replay.

criteria.note: At intake, canonicalize and SHA-256 hash the service definition, exact query manifest, every returned page, aggregate snapshot, and each normalized candidate row.

evidence.note: The publisher states that certified perimeters and new perimeters beginning in 2021 are included and that data before 2021 are incomplete.
Required incident IDs, state, type, final-report date, fire-out date, final acres, complex membership, and polygon geometry fields exist.

criteria.note: Fit only as the incident-identity and maturity authority for 2021-2022. It is not the complete candidate universe and does not provide scientific labels.

evidence.note: The public schema was inspected without credentials. The proposed allowlist omits usernames, personnel, costs, and free-text operational fields.

criteria.note: Query only the approved incident, maturity, identity, complex, state, area, timestamp, and geometry allowlist. No credentials or nonpublic services are permitted.

sources.name: Monitoring Trends in Burn Severity Burned Areas Boundaries, version 12.0, April 2025

evidence.note: ScienceBase item identifies version 12.0, April 2025, last revision 2025-04-22, and coverage through 2024.

criteria.note: Exact file is mtbs_perims_DD.zip, 374,092,911 bytes, publisher MD5 65278fcb893f94cd0eaf66d966ee7125.

evidence.note: USGS identifies MTBS as the USGS EROS and USDA Forest Service GTAC interagency burn-mapping program.

criteria.note: Authoritative for the exact completed MTBS inventory and reference-availability record, not for ground truth.

evidence.note: Public ScienceBase metadata provides an anonymous HTTPS file locator, size, format, and checksum.

criteria.note: No account, credential, click-through, or cost was observed for the proposed exact archive.

evidence.note: USGS marks the MTBS information public domain and states that MTBS data are freely available to the public.
USGS-authored data and information are public domain in the United States; USGS requests source acknowledgement.

criteria.note: Retain MTBS, USGS, and USDA Forest Service attribution and version identity in every derived artifact.

evidence.note: ScienceBase records USGS and USDA Forest Service originators, USGS publisher, EROS data owner, file metadata, and publication and revision dates.

criteria.note: The exact ScienceBase item and file, not the mutable rolling MTBS download URL, are the proposed custody source.

evidence.note: Publisher supplies file size 374,092,911 and MD5 65278fcb893f94cd0eaf66d966ee7125.

criteria.note: Controlled intake must verify publisher MD5, compute SHA-256, validate ZIP members and shapefile structure, and retain the original bytes read-only.

evidence.note: MTBS consistently maps large western fires at 1,000 acres or greater and produces 30 m products.
The publisher says 2023-2025 mapping remains in progress; 2021-2022 avoids that declared completion boundary.
FGDC metadata exposes exact identity, fire type, mapped area, centroid, ignition date, mapping program, and geometry fields.

criteria.note: Fit as the versioned universe and reference-availability registry. It is source-dependent remote-sensing evidence, omits unmappable fires, and cannot be called independent ground truth. Threshold, index, scene, and analyst-comment fields are explicitly denied from selection intake.

evidence.note: The proposed shapefile fields are public fire metadata and geometry; no credential, secret, personal, or regulated-data requirement was observed.

criteria.note: Use a strict field allowlist and reject free-text comments and all dNBR, NBR, RdNBR, threshold, scene-selection, label, and metric fields from the eligibility pipeline.

evidence.note: UMM metadata binds provider LPCLOUD, collection identifiers, temporal coverage, format, related documentation, DOI, and current known-issues document.

criteria.note: Retain CMR concept and revision, query bytes, granule concept and revision IDs, native IDs, temporal and spatial metadata, and access timestamps.

evidence.note: The official catalog identifies global 30 m daily HLSL30 surface reflectance, common gridding, QA, and temporal coverage beginning 2013-04-11.

criteria.note: Fit for metadata-level pre/post availability checks. Granule presence is not a cloud-free observation, usable composite, registration pass, or dataset-readiness result.

evidence.note: Public collection metadata contains no personal, regulated, or secret-bearing fields needed by the proposed query.

criteria.note: Use anonymous metadata endpoints only in M1. Do not collect, log, or expose Earthdata credentials.

sources.name: EPA Level III Ecoregions of the Conterminous United States, no-state-boundary archive

evidence.note: EPA identifies the current Level III no-state-boundary shapefile and its metadata.
HEAD returned 28,424,315 bytes, Last-Modified 2024-11-14T17:09:20Z, and multipart ETag 2c2e9e749597f2b4d5553586cb6d23ff-2.

criteria.note: Dataset metadata identifies publication date 2013-04-16 and an as-needed maintenance status. The current publisher-linked archive is the proposed exact locator.

evidence.note: EPA documents the Level III ecoregion framework and its multi-agency derivation and intended ecological stratification use.

criteria.note: Authoritative for the EPA Level III ecological-region classification.

evidence.note: The publisher-linked 28 MB ZIP is anonymously available over HTTPS with no observed account, credential, cost, or click-through.

criteria.note: Acquire once through controlled no-overwrite intake after owner approval.

evidence.note: FGDC metadata states no access or use constraints and says EPA acknowledgement is appreciated.
EPA states that EPA-produced geospatial data are public domain by default unless otherwise specified.

criteria.note: Retain EPA source acknowledgement, archive identity, metadata, and scale limitations.

evidence.note: FGDC metadata records EPA originator, ORD/NHEERL publisher, publication date, methods, source literature, coordinate system, attributes, and revision notes.

criteria.note: Retain source metadata and exact archive alongside the derived dominant-code and coverage fields.

evidence.note: HTTP metadata supplies exact byte length, last-modified time, and a multipart ETag that is retained as a locator identity but is not treated as a content checksum.

criteria.note: Controlled intake must compute SHA-256, validate ZIP and shapefile structure, inspect the embedded metadata, and preserve exact bytes read-only.

evidence.note: Level III polygons cover the conterminous United States and are intended for broad areas such as states, multiple counties, and river basins at 1:250,000 digitizing scale.

criteria.note: Fit only for event-level ecological stratification and coverage checks, not local ecological truth, pixel labels, or fine-scale management claims.

evidence.note: FGDC metadata classifies the public geospatial data as having no confidentiality and standard technical controls.

criteria.note: No personal, regulated, credential, executable, or secret-bearing content is required. Validate the archive before processing.
